svg.text: Quantization mechanics: the map, the error bound, and where it breaks
A — Symmetric INT8: lay 255 evenly spaced levels across [−max|w|, +max|w|]
s = max|w| / 127 (the SCALE — one float kept per tensor/channel/group)
q = round(w / s) (store this: one signed byte, −127…127)
ŵ = s · q (DEQUANTIZE back to float when needed)
Error is bounded by half a step: |w − ŵ| ≤ s/2. Always. No exceptions, no accumulation within one weight.
255 levels, step s = 0.254/127 = 0.0020 — the grid any weight must snap to
B — One real weight row, quantized and back (8 of a 4096-wide row)
max |err| = 0.0008 ≤ s/2 = 0.0010 ✓ — worst case 0.3% of the row's range. 16 bytes became 8 bytes + one scale.
C — Why a 0.3% perturbation on every weight barely moves the output
1. Precision for integrating ≠ for reporting
FP16's 10 mantissa bits were needed to
ACCUMULATE gradient updates of ~1e-5
relative, over trillions of steps. Inference
just reads the finished value.
EE framing: a high-resolution ADC to
integrate a drifting signal; far fewer bits
to report the settled result.
2. The error is INCOHERENT
y = Σ wᵢxᵢ over 4096 terms. Rounding
errors δᵢ are independent and zero-mean,
so they partly cancel (grow as √n) while
the signal grows as √n too —
output relative error ≈ weight relative
error. It does NOT amplify.
Across 32 layers it compounds only ~√32.
3. Trained networks sit in flat regions of the loss surface and were trained amid noise (SGD, dropout, BF16
arithmetic). Small weight perturbations are the condition they were optimized under, not a novel insult.
D — Where it breaks: OUTLIERS waste the level budget
Weights: well-behaved, bell-shaped
range ≈ ±0.25 → all 255 levels used
INT8 here is near-lossless.
Activations above ~6.7B params: outlier features
~0.1% of dims,
20–100× larger
one per-tensor scale is set by the far-right spike →
the real mass is crushed into ~3 of 255 levels.
Mitigations — all of them are "stop sharing one scale across things with different magnitudes":
• finer granularity: per-channel, or per-GROUP (64 or 128 weights share a scale) — the standard fix for weights
• mixed decomposition (LLM.int8): keep the ~0.1% outlier dimensions in FP16, everything else INT8
• SmoothQuant: migrate the scale difficulty out of activations into weights, where it is tolerable
Smarter rounding — not every weight deserves equal treatment:
• GPTQ: round layer by layer, minimizing the layer's OUTPUT error (second-order), not the weight error
• AWQ (activation-aware): protect the weights that multiply large activations; they matter more
• NF4 (NormalFloat-4): place the 16 levels at a normal distribution's quantiles, not uniformly — fits the shape
